title: Dialogue, Reasoning, and Comparative Method — Part 542

sentences.en: Sheikh: Certainly there must have been some reason for that.

But why should we
worry about the mutual discord of our elders?
Why should we pry into their differences after 1300 years?

Well-Wisher: When you cannot find a reasonable answer to prove your point, you depend upon such a
reply.
But before all fair minded people, the matter is too clear to require any elucidation or proof.

As for your assertion that we need not interfere in the differences of our predecessors, of course you are
right, insofar as their affairs have no bearing on us.

But in the present case you are mistaken because it
is the duty of every sensible Muslim to have faith based on reason, not on blind following.

In making
inquiries regarding religion, we study the common history of the Muslims.
We find that, after the death of the Holy Prophet, two sects appeared.

Therefore, we should make
thorough inquiries in order to understand which of the two sects is rightly guided.

Obviously we should
not blindly follow our predecessors.
Sheikh: Certainly your point is that Abu Bakr's caliphate was not just.

But if Abu Bakr was not the rightful
Caliph, and if it was the right of ‘Ali to occupy that position, why did he not use his special strength and
courage to establish justice?
